skill.name: schema-research
skill.description: Researches official Schema.org classes and properties for Logseq Template Graph. It explains hierarchy, type mapping, missing properties, and integration steps for template expansion.
skill.summary: Research Schema.org classes and properties for Logseq template design.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: The static findings are documentation examples, Schema.org reference URLs, and small browser-opening helper scripts. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, destructive commands, hidden exfiltration, or reconnaissance behavior. The scripts still warrant disclosure because they launch a browser and rely on network access to Schema.org.

remediation.issue: Optional helper scripts open external URLs in a browser.
remediation.suggestion: Document that the scripts are optional and validate lookup terms before opening a Schema.org page.

remediation.issue: Network access is central to current Schema.org lookups.
remediation.suggestion: State clearly that the skill fetches Schema.org pages and avoid adding unrelated external endpoints.

remediation.issue: Markdown code fences trigger static command warnings.
remediation.suggestion: Use plain-text examples where possible or label examples as documentation-only to reduce false alarms.

static_findings.snippet: - List all properties for a given class
- Suggest missing properties for a class
- Search existing template for the class

content.value_statement: Schema.org changes make template design hard to verify. This skill fetches official vocabulary and maps classes and properties to Logseq patterns.
actual_capabilities: Looks up Schema.org class and property pages using official URLs.
Summarizes inheritance, child classes, sibling classes, and inherited properties.
Maps Schema.org value types to Logseq property types and cardinality.
Compares requested classes or properties with existing template modules.
Suggests module placement, reusable properties, and phased integration steps.
Provides research examples for common Schema.org expansion tasks.
limitations: Latest results require network access to Schema.org.
It does not guarantee Schema.org pages are complete or unchanged.
The documented workflow focuses on research, not automatic file edits.
Helper scripts only open Schema.org pages; they do not validate template content.

use_cases.title: Evaluate New Classes
use_cases.description: A maintainer checks whether Recipe, Event, or MedicalCondition fits the current module structure.

use_cases.title: Audit Missing Properties
use_cases.description: A data modeler compares existing Person fields with Schema.org and ranks additions by reuse value.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation Notes
use_cases.description: A documentation writer turns research into clear module guidance and usage examples.

prompt_templates.title: Research a Class
prompt_templates.prompt: Research the Schema.org Recipe class and explain whether it belongs in the creative-work module.

prompt_templates.title: Find Property Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare our Person template with Schema.org Person and list missing high-value properties.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Type Mapping
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate birthDate for Logseq. Include expected Schema.org type, cardinality, and the recommended Logseq property type.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Module Expansion
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a module expansion for MedicalCondition. Include hierarchy, dependent classes, reusable properties, risks, and a phased implementation order.

output_examples.output: A concise report identifies Recipe as a CreativeWork subtype, lists core cooking properties, and recommends the creative-work module.

output_examples.input: What are we missing for Person?
output: Short reasons for each recommended field.
A phased plan for template updates.

output_examples.input: Should birthDate use date or default?
output_examples.output: The answer recommends a date property, explains Schema.org Date expectations, and notes query benefits in Logseq.

best_practices: Fetch the official Schema.org page before recommending a class or property.
Check existing modules first so inherited or shared properties are not duplicated.
Record the reason for each type, cardinality, and module placement decision.
anti_patterns: Adding a property because the name seems useful without checking Schema.org.
Duplicating inherited properties in every class instead of reusing common fields.
Treating helper script output as validation of the Logseq template.

faq.question: Can this skill research any Schema.org class?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a class or property name and it will use Schema.org as the primary source.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: Yes for current Schema.org information. Local reference files can still guide structure when offline.

faq.question: Does it change my Logseq files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives research and integration guidance unless you separately request file edits.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What makes it different from a basic web search?
faq.answer: It connects Schema.org details to Logseq modules, property types, cardinality, and reuse decisions.

faq.question: Are the helper scripts required?
faq.answer: No. They are optional shortcuts that open Schema.org pages in a browser.
